approval_scope: P12-A host-only scheduling-policy contract v01 as a design/contract proposal only; authorizes writing the policy source, the 24 declared tests, and the frozen verification plan under Option A (no new canonical acceptance gates). It does not authorize runtime scheduler use, production module/assembly/IRQ/TSS/allocator/runner changes, P12-B/C, deployment, or any Phase12 completion claim.

areas.name: approved Phase12 design lineage and scope
areas.findings: design.md raw SHA256 fe57e4a8...a880 matches the approved pin and the task-stated approved hash. Contract cites design sections 4/8 (lines 41-49/83-85), section 3:28 (no production module/assembly/IRQ/TSS/allocator/runner changes), and section 9:95 (A's acceptance contract is separately approved choice, not mandatory gates) — all verified present in design.md with matching content. F5 prerequisite HEAD d9cebe28eb5139b6b614b7000688857361e2afc4 equals live git HEAD (verified via git rev-parse). Scope is host-only P12-A per design section 3/10; no production implementation claim. preflight_01.json exists locally as cited.

areas.name: exact P12-A policy semantics (states, transitions, selection, fairness, inhibition, capacity)
areas.findings: States {Unused,Ready,Running,Retired} and Context {Idle,Worker(u8)} match design section 4 exactly (UNUSED->READY->RUNNING->READY/RETIRED, no reuse/reclaim). Selection: yield re-appends current at FIFO tail, dequeue head, empty selects Idle; matches design round-robin rule. Idle never queued, exactly-one-current invariant stated. Admission does not switch idle immediately — a deliberate, explicitly justified refinement of the design, not a contradiction. Inhibition: reschedule while inhibited only latches pending; final leave drains pending exactly once — matches design 'inhibited reschedule only latches a pending decision'. Fairness claim is correctly bounded to uninhibited repeated requests (each worker selected within 2 decisions), with no fairness claim while inhibited or for arbitrary future runtime. TaskKind labels (KernelProbe only; Cpl3/F5 refuse UnsupportedKind) honor the design's 'no resume F5/CPL3 request' refusal.

areas.name: capacity and bounds
areas.findings: Two slots, ready-queue cap 2, u8 IDs 1..=254 with 0 reserved and 255 reserved invalid, checked u8 inhibit depth max 255 with InhibitOverflow/InhibitUnderflow refusals (no wrap/saturation), metadata budget size_of::<Policy>()<=1024 asserted as a test, all queue arithmetic exact over 2 cells. Consistent with design's two-worker/idle cap and <=1024-byte budget (design says the budget is a future compile-time/test assertion; contract makes it test 22 — consistent).

areas.name: determinism
areas.findings: Admission order fixes FIFO tie-breaking; no priority/quantum/ticks/nondeterministic input; no randomness, time, or environment reads; test 24 replays a fixed legal sequence on two fresh models and compares literal alternating IDs (model-to-model, not implementation-to-itself). Exhaustive length-4 trace enumeration (8 ops, 4096 traces) is finite and deterministic.

areas.name: no_std compatibility
areas.findings: Plan proves no_std via standalone rustc --crate-type lib with a dedicated wrapper applying #![no_std] + #[path] to the exact source; source itself uses only core/primitives. No dependencies, unsafe, asm, ports, atomics, locks, panic!/unreachable!, recursion, or global state. This is a concrete verifiable plan, not an asserted fact.

areas.name: allocation-free implementation plan
areas.findings: Policy holds a private fixed Snapshot ([Slot;2], [u8;2], u8 counters, bool); no Vec/String/heap, no references or globals; Snapshot/Slot/enums are Copy/Eq so returns transfer no resources. Private helpers bounded to scans of 2 slots and 2 queue cells. Tests may allocate bounded traces — acceptable since the no-allocation constraint is on the policy core, matching design section 4 ('no heap allocations inside the policy core').

areas.name: all error/refusal semantics
areas.findings: Error enum covers InvalidId, UnknownId, DuplicateId, RetiredId, Capacity, InvalidTransition, UnsupportedKind, Inhibited, InhibitOverflow, InhibitUnderflow — a superset of the design's refusal list (unknown/out-of-range IDs, duplicate enqueue, invalid transition, over-cap admission, retired reuse, F5-resume refusal) with checked nesting. Precedence is fully specified per operation (numeric ID validation first, then kind/duplicate/retired/inhibit/capacity for admit; UnknownId/RetiredId/InvalidTransition/Inhibited for complete). Every Err path preserves the entire Snapshot (nonmutating refusals per design). Conservative additions (admission-while-inhibited refuses) are explicitly labeled as proposed choices requiring reviewer approval — appropriate for a contract review.

areas.name: logical task lifetime
areas.findings: Retired slots/IDs stay consumed forever in an instance; fresh Policy construction is the only reset and is explicitly not reuse of real kernel IDs/resources; RETIRED makes no frame-release/IRQ-detach/CPU-stack claim (matches design section 4's logical-only caveat). pending implies depth>0 and final leave always clears pending — instance-local invariants closed.

areas.name: exact test identities and logical RED plan
areas.findings: 24 exact #[test] names with p12a_policy_tests:: prefix; extracted from the contract and compared programmatically against filter_audit_01.json new_exact_identities — exact ordered match, zero new ignored. Coverage maps to design section 8 host categories (empty/idle, FIFO, one-current, duplicate refusal, unknown IDs, retired/no-reuse, capacity, invalid edges, inhibit overflow/underflow, no-switch-while-inhibited/pending drain, F5-resume refusal, zero-allocation/nonmutating). Logical RED plan is genuine: tests registered before implementation, inert labeled red scaffold that compiles/lists 24/executes but admits nothing, with literal expected-outcome assertions (e.g. Ready vs Unused) so RED is a real assertion failure, not an import error; scaffold preserved as raw source and never frozen as candidate.

areas.name: inherited filter isolation
areas.findings: filter_audit_01.json records zero filter_collisions and zero name_collisions. Independently verified: none of the 24 new names contains any of the 19 inherited filter literals as substring/prefix, and no baseline host identity contains 'p12a'. Baseline report shows exactly 394 unique host identities (392 passed + the 2 documented maintenance_measurements ignores) and 149 unique B26 identities; new host set = baseline + exactly 24. B26 is separately rooted, not a colliding host prefix. No inherited identity shrinks or is edited.

areas.name: Class T/P decision and baseline-ELF plan
areas.findings: Baseline b01/report.json: overall PASS, reproducible=true, both production A/B ELFs built before source/tests with cargo +nightly build at repository CWD, default features, no CARGO/RUST env vars, kernel-only cargo clean between; both raw ELF hashes 981f373a...54e4 verified on-disk and equal each other and the accepted F5 final linked ELF in FINAL_REPORT.md ('Exact final linked production ELF 981f...'). Class T requires A=B=AFTER plus complete module/source/symbol proof (objdump discovery via existing f3_full_guest tooling), not source alone; mismatch gives one bounded look then Class P with contract revision before implementation verification. Skipped F1-F5 matrices (10/8/18/12/12 at 128/512MiB) must be listed explicitly, never called fresh PASS; Class P invalidates the skip. Sound.

areas.name: production isolation verification
areas.findings: Placement is tests_kernel-only via #[path] pub mod in tests_kernel/src/lib.rs mirroring F5 lib.rs:52-56 convention; src/main.rs production module graph and bin-only Cargo manifest exclude the source; no production mod/use/reexport/static/function-pointer/asm/runtime hook. Verification records module graph, all p12a references across src (incl. .s), tests_kernel, scripts, manifests, and confirms no p12a symbols in the production ELF via the actual LLVM objdump location. Matches design section 10 ('add no crate, kernel module, asm, IRQ/TSS/allocator change').

areas.name: proposed preservation scope and mock-gate rule
areas.findings: Preservation: inherited 394/149 identities and all inherited filters/gates unchanged; protected hashes, source-before=after, F5 predecessor identity/gate multiset readback, parent artifact integrity readback all required. Mock gate REQUIRED because phase6_verify.source_snapshot():450-490 enumerates the two new .rs files plus modified tests_kernel/src/lib.rs — snapshot membership 234->236 is an expected observation to verify, not a fabricated pass; harness runs with unchanged 1049s limit only for that gate (consistent with design section 9's 'approved 1049s limit remains mock-only'). Freeze includes actual canonical source snapshot and all inputs with no assumed pin count; no live mutable STATE pinned (immutable snapshots) — correctly avoids the historical F5 STATE-drift defect.

areas.name: acceptance-gate decision
areas.findings: Option A: host-only verified milestone with NO new canonical acceptance gates; no canonical run/readback, no runner/validator edits; F5 PASS76 remains a historical exact predecessor, not a fresh P12-A claim. This is consistent with design section 9:95 which leaves A's acceptance-contract extension as a separately approved choice rather than mandatory. The contract still mandates comprehensive (not metadata-only) candidate review and full frozen host/B26/fmt/no_std/ELF checks. Accepting Option A at contract level is the correct decision for this milestone.

areas.name: historical predecessor limitations
areas.findings: Contract preserves: F1 independent final canonical readback never produced (no retroactive claim); F3 one-nested-NMI 2578/16384B is a conditional static bound, not high-water/unlimited recursion; F5 terminal CPL3-only/IF0/PIC-masked/nonresumable proof unchanged; no NX/W^X guarantee. Cross-checked against FINAL_REPORT.md sections 'Limits and Phase12 boundary', 'Emitted closure and bounds', and 'Additional explicit proof limits' — faithful, no broadened guarantees. The F5 evidence_manifest's FINAL_REPORT artifact binding an older historical_self_bound revision is called out explicitly so current report bytes are never falsely compared to that old digest — a real trap the contract handles correctly.

areas.name: P12-B boundary
areas.findings: P12-B requires its own bounded ABI/stack/lifetime design, prerequisite resolution, independent design approval, and fresh explicit user authorization; 'Stop after A' closes the milestone. Matches design sections 5/10 (new reviewed call/return ABI, owned guarded stacks, separate authorization) and the stage table's 'P12-B/C are design directions with blockers, NOT implementation-ready authorizations'. No P12-B/C scope leak into A.

evidence_sufficiency: Not metadata-only: verified 9/9 manifest pins by recomputing raw SHA256 of every pinned file (all match), recomputed the manifest's own raw SHA256, confirmed baseline A/B ELF files on disk hash to the pinned value and equal the accepted F5 ELF, confirmed reproducible=true and git_status_before==git_status_after in b01/report.json, counted 394 unique host / 149 unique B26 baseline identities with the 2 documented ignores, extracted the 24 contract test names and matched them exactly to filter_audit_01.json, and programmatically confirmed zero substring/prefix collisions between the 24 new names and the 19 inherited filter literals.
notes: The manifest's review_inputs_01 pin points to test_results/phase12_design/review_inputs_01.json (the approved Phase12 design review manifest) — correct lineage pin, not the P12-A manifest itself.

Contract's 'All39 review manifest pins and 30 inventory inputs verified (preflight_01.json)' is a preflight claim; preflight_01.json exists locally.
